memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And Abimelek asked Abraham, "What was your reason for doing this?" Abraham replied, "I said to myself, 'There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'" - Gen 20:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Confronted, Abraham explains his reasoning: "I said to myself, 'There is surely no fear of God in this place.'" He had assumed the worst about Gerar - that these were godless people who would kill him to take his wife. So he lied to protect himself. But his assumption was wrong. As we've just seen, Abimelech feared God more than Abraham did in that moment.

Notice the root of Abraham's failure: a fearful assumption. He looked at a place and concluded there was "no fear of God" there - and acted out of that fear rather than out of trust. His whole scheme was built on a judgement about others that turned out to be false.

How often we do the same. We assume the worst about a person, a place, a situation, and then act out of that fearful assumption. We decide in advance that we must protect ourselves, that no one here can be trusted, that God cannot be trusted to handle this - and our fear leads us into sin.

But God is often already at work in places we've written off as godless. Abraham underestimated what God was doing in Gerar. We may underestimate what He is doing in the people and places we fear. Rather than acting out of anxious assumptions, we are called to trust God and act with integrity. "Do not be anxious about anything" (Phil 4:6). Fear tells us to protect ourselves by compromise; faith tells us to trust God and do right.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you making fearful assumptions about a person or situation?
- How might fear be leading you toward compromise instead of trust?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, forgive me for the fearful assumptions that lead me into sin. Help me not to write off people and places as beyond Your reach. Give me faith to trust You and act with integrity, not fear.
Amen.
